Key Takeaways

Meta Platforms launched $35 billion of stock offerings on Monday and plans a separate $60 billion program in 2027, on the same day Anthropic reportedly planned to file publicly for its IPO.

Jim Cramer warns that Anthropic's listing will pull money away from the rest of the AI group, a group that includes Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet.

Nvidia's forward P/E is at 17x, the low of its three-year range, even though analysts' estimate of its fiscal 2028 earnings has risen 25% since the end of June.

Microsoft looks the most exposed: it trades at 27x forward earnings, and its three-year low is 19x.

AI investors are about to be asked for a lot more money.

On Monday, Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) launched $35 billion of stock offerings. That same morning, Anthropic planned to make its IPO filing public, Bloomberg reported. The Claude maker reportedly expects its IPO to match or beat the size of SpaceX's.

Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) wants a piece of Meta's deal too. It's one of three chipmakers that said they might buy up to $5 billion of Meta's new shares, though none of them has committed.

Jim Cramer saw this problem coming. On Mad Money a week ago, he warned that Anthropic's listing will "suck a massive amount of money away from the rest of the group" just because Anthropic is so big.

That group includes Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ), Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) and Alphabet (GOOG), and all three report earnings this week.

And Meta is just getting started.

Meta's share count is headed the other way

For years, Meta has been shrinking its diluted share count. It fell about 10% from fiscal 2021 to fiscal 2025, to 2.57 billion.

Meta Platforms (META): diluted shares outstanding, billions of shares, fiscal 2021–2025 (TIKR)

Now Meta is adding stock. The new deals are $22.5 billion of Class A shares and about $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred stock, with a separate $60 billion at-the-market program planned for 2027. Meta expects $135 billion to $145 billion of capex this year. It plans to pay for that with operating cash flow, investment-grade debt, partnerships and new stock.

Daniel Niles, a veteran tech investor, pointed out on X that Meta said in a recent filing that everyone is competing for the same pool of money. In his view, that pool "no longer seems endless like it did back earlier in the year."

title: 1 Reason to Buy Meta Stock Now and Hold for the Long Term

1 Reason to Buy Meta Stock Now and Hold for the Long Term
John Ballard, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 3:20 PM EDT 3 min read
META
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), the owner of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, makes nearly all of its money from ads. As of Oct. 22, the stock is down about 10% from its September high of $779.82. This is despite a strong third-quarter earnings report, with revenue growing 26% year over year.

One reason I see the dip as a buying opportunity is that Meta is building new revenue streams that could make it an even stronger business over time. Meta's non-ad revenue from its apps grew 59% to $1.1 billion. Management said this growth came mainly from WhatsApp paid messaging -- businesses paying to message their customers on the app -- and subscriptions.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Another non-advertising revenue stream is Meta One, a subscription service that unlocks extra features across the company's apps, which has passed 15 million subscriptions and trials. That's less than 2% of Meta's total revenue today, but it's growing more than twice as fast as the company overall.

Image source: Getty Images.

The runway is long. Meta estimates at least 500 million small businesses use its apps to reach customers, a ready-made market for paid messaging and AI business tools. CFO Susan Li said the company is starting new AI businesses that could start contributing to revenue growth in 2027, with the potential to scale "meaningfully" over the long term.

The main near-term headwind for the stock is heavy spending: Meta plans to spend up to $145 billion on capital expenditures this year, but management expects strong revenue growth to continue in 2027.

Meta stock trades at about 19 times analysts' 2027 earnings estimate -- roughly in line with the S&P 500's average forward multiple of 19.3. I believe that's a reasonable price for a business with a daily user base of over 3.6 billion and the ability to reach new users through AI services over time.

title: Anthropic's IPO Keeps Founders in Control Through a "Founder LLC" Voting Structure
detail:
Anthropic's IPO Keeps Founders in Control Through a "Founder LLC" Voting Structure
Anders Bylund, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 4:17 PM EDT 6 min read
NVDA
ANTH.PVT
GOOG
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The initial public offering (IPO) queue just welcomed its most unconventional corporate creature yet. Artificial intelligence (AI) heavyweight Anthropic, the developer behind the Claude platform, officially filed its Form S-1 registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) today.

The filing sets the stage for a Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT. But beneath Anthropic's staggering compute numbers and explosive top-line growth lies a governance framework that should stop prospective shareholders in their tracks.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Silicon Valley has long treated public investors as passive passengers. Mega-cap innovators like Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), and Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) built modern market empires on dual- or triple-class equities. Their stock structures grant public buyers economic claims while effectively walling off boardroom power behind insider shares.

But Anthropic's proposed setup makes even those founder-friendly bastions look tame. Instead of merely weighting voting rights based on who owns the most stock, Anthropic is slicing ownership, shareholder voting, and board oversight into five distinct share classes.

Data from Anthropic's S-1 filing.

The 4 Major Differences
1. A single "golden share" instead of billions of shares (Class F)

SpaceX and Meta are the same story. Musk and Zuckerberg both have total control over shareholder votes through their massive holdings of supervoting Class B shares. They have the option to convert these shares into common stock if they want to raise personal cash, but then they would gradually lose their voting power.

At Anthropic, the founders created Class F common stock consisting of a single share held by the founders' LLC. It has no economic rights (no claim to profits or dividends) but gives the co-founders 50.1% of the total vote on all general corporate matters. The vote counts of other classes don't even matter in most cases; Class F decides the outcome of simple-majority votes.

title: Scott Galloway Picks Meta as AI’s “Big Winner” as Its $35 Billion Raise Lifts the Stock

Scott Galloway Picks Meta as AI’s “Big Winner” as Its $35 Billion Raise Lifts the Stock
Roxanna Maglangit
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 2:37 PM EDT 5 min read
META
Trade META on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Scott Galloway Picks Meta as AI's "Big Winner" as Its $35 Billion Raise Lifts the Stock ©Rido via Canva
Key Takeaways

Meta launched about $35 billion of common and convertible preferred stock on Monday, and shares rose after falling 9% the week before.

Scott Galloway named Meta the likely "big winner" of the AI boom, pointing to its moats and its capital for the AI arms race.

Meta's ad business grew revenue to $201 billion in 2025, but this year's spending has outrun its cash, and another $60 billion share program is planned for 2027.

At 20x forward earnings, below its three-year average of 23x, the stock isn't priced like an AI winner, and the 2027 spending plan in late January is the next test.

Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) just launched the stock sale investors had been bracing for, and shares are up [1%] today.

The offerings come to about $35 billion, to pay for Meta's AI build: roughly $22.5 billion of Class A common stock and $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred, according to its filing. Shares slid early, then turned higher, after a 9% drop in a week on its spending plans.

And they landed the same day Scott Galloway made a call he clearly didn't enjoy making.

On the latest episode of Prof G Markets, which he co-hosts, Galloway asked which company, three years from now, "we'll look back and think that was the big winner of this AI boom." His pick was Meta, which he said "has the biggest moats, has the capital to engage in this arms race."

His own verdict: "I hate to admit it, it's Mark Zuckerberg and Meta right now."

The wait is over

The raise itself was no surprise. Janus Henderson's Alison Porter told Bloomberg Tech last Thursday that "we do think this is going to be an overhang on the stock through until we see that capital raise actually occur." She expected it "sometime in Q1."

It came four days later.

The ads pay for the arms race

Galloway's point about capital starts with the ad business. Advertising brought in $196.2 billion of Meta's $201.0 billion of revenue in 2025, and total revenue grew 70% from 2021 to 2025.

Meta Platforms (META): total revenues, $ billions, fiscal 2021–2025 (TIKR)

And it's still growing fast. Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, and management guides the fourth quarter to $73 billion to $76 billion, 22% to 27% above a year earlier. Its apps reached 3.64 billion people a day on average in September.

Tech stocks were higher late Monday afternoon, with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) rising 1.7% and the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) adding 2.1%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index climbed 2.7%.

In sector news, Anthropic on Monday filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission for an IPO of class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT."

In corporate news, SpaceX (SPCX) entered into a lease agreement totaling about $40 billion with an Apollo Global Management-managed (APO) entity, under which it will obtain graphics processing unit pods and equipment for its data centers, SpaceX said Monday in a regulatory filing. SpaceX shares were down 0.1%.

Meta Platforms (META) said Monday it launched about $35 billion in stock offerings and plans a separate $60 billion at-the-market share sale program in 2027 as part of a financing plan to support its AI investments and other corporate purposes. Meta shares were down 2.1%.

Microsoft (MSFT) plans to offer buyouts to roughly 60,000 workers, with staff on select teams in the US, Canada, India and the UK at the vice president level and below, Bloomberg reported Monday, citing a spokesperson. Microsoft shares rose 1.5%.

Apple (AAPL) said Monday it is rolling out a new iPad mini with an 8.5-inch OLED screen and A20 Pro chip. Apple shares were down 1.1%.
